article.story: No. 20 Houston (7-3) at West Virginia (5-5), Nov. 21 at 1 p.m. EST. Opening Line: Houston by 7.5. Against the spread: Houston 3-7, West Virginia 5-4-1. How to watch: TNT Key stats Houston Offense Overall: 470.9 yards per game (11th in FBS) Passing: 263.5 yards per game (25th) Rushing: 207.4 yards per game (20th) Scoring: 35.1 points per game (19th) Houston Defense Overall: 370.8 yards per game (82nd in FBS) Passing: 249.3 yards per game (125th) Rushing: 121.5 yards per game (35th) Scoring: 23.4 points per game (60th) West Virginia Offense Overall: 458.9 yards per game (13th in FBS) Passing: 218.2 yards per game (77th) Rushing: 240.7 yards per game (6th) Scoring: 34.9 points per game (20th) West Virginia Defense Overall: 495.7 yards per game (137th in FBS) Passing: 305.7 yards per game (138th) Rushing: 190 yards per game (121st) Scoring: 34.8 points per game (131st) West Virginia ranks 114th in defensive third down percentage, allowing opponents to convert 45.4% of the time. Houston ranks 1st on offense, converting on 58.9% of third downs. Houston is 17th in the FBS with a +6 turnover margin. Houston is 107th in FBS in red zone defense, allowing opponents to score on 88.9% of trips. West Virginia's red zone offense ranks 36th, scoring on 88.6% of red zone opportunities. West Virginia is 126th in the FBS with an average time of possession of 27:43, compared to Houston's 20th-ranked average of 32:08. Team leaders Houston Passing: Conner Weigman, 2,552 yards, 25 TDs, 3 INTs, 65.6 completion percentage Rushing: Makhi Hughes, 712 yards on 144 carries, 5 TDs Receiving: Amare Thomas, 764 yards on 53 catches, 9 TDs West Virginia Passing: Michael Hawkins Jr., 2,128 yards, 13 TDs, 3 INTs, 57.4 completion percentage Rushing: Cam Cook, 1,084 yards on 218 carries, 8 TDs Receiving: D.J. Epps, 615 yards on 28 catches, 5 TDs Last game Houston fell 42-32 to Colorado on Nov. 13. Weigman led Houston with 272 yards on 26-of-42 passing (61.9%) for three touchdowns and one interception. He also carried the ball six times for 29 yards. Hughes carried the ball 15 times for 106 yards and scored one touchdown, adding two receptions for 23 yards. Patrick Overmyer put up 116 yards on nine catches with one touchdown. West Virginia fell to Kansas 37-14 on Nov. 14. Hawkins led West Virginia with 227 yards on 19-of-34 passing (55.9%) for one touchdown and one interception. He also carried the ball 25 times for 36 yards and one rushing touchdown. Cook had 12 rushing yards on nine carries, adding one reception for eight yards. Epps had five receptions for 51 yards. Next game Houston hosts Baylor on Nov. 28. West Virginia plays at No. 2 Utah on Nov. 27.
